notes: Weights are warmed separately; measured requests start with an empty prompt cache.
TTFT includes prefill, save, transfer, restore, and final prompt evaluation.
Repeats alternate local/split and split/local using identical canonical tokens.
Five repeats do not support a reliable tail-latency (p95) estimate.
A supported TTFT win requires the lower 95% paired bootstrap interval to exceed 1.
Memory shows before/after snapshots and sampled peaks provided by the runtime.
Sampled peaks can miss short transients; inspect sampling period/count.
Canonical corpus tokenization is preparation time, outside measured request TTFT.
Native prefill throughput counts N tokens locally and N-1 remotely before handoff.

Modeled ideal 1Gbps is an optimistic projection, not a LAN measurement: split TTFT − measured transfer time + state bytes / 125,000,000 × 1,000 ms. Other observed overhead stays unchanged. The replacement assumes payload-only 1,000 Mbit/s and omits transport framing, checksum and disk costs inside the measured transfer timer. Its paired CI describes sample variation under this fixed assumption, not real-link uncertainty or evidence of a measured win.
Dashboard phase updates occur after each sample to keep rendering outside timed requests.
Scope reduced by user from five to four pairs, with all eight requested measurements complete; original cancellation report is preserved in long-context-20261012/4b-benchmark.json.
The separate network probe used 64 MiB per direction with three repeats and includes fresh SSH setup and hashing. State-transfer timing here measures the application path.
Warmup used only 32 tokens per mode. No full-length warmup or cold-disk claim is made. Mac memory admission was explicitly waived; CUDA guards remained enabled.
